title: How to Clean Up After Rodents in the Attic
h1: How to Clean Up After Rodents in Your Attic
description: Rodent cleanup in the attic means removing droppings safely, replacing soiled insulation, sanitizing and sealing entry points. Here's how the job gets done.
quick_answer: Clean up after rodents only once they're gone and entry points are sealed. Ventilate the space, wear a respirator and gloves, soak droppings and urine with disinfectant before wiping them up, and never sweep or dry-vacuum them. Contaminated insulation usually needs to be removed, the attic sanitized and fresh insulation installed. Heavy infestations are best handled by a professional crew.
body:
Why is rodent cleanup more than tidying up?

Rats and mice leave behind droppings, urine, nesting material and sometimes dead animals. Their waste can carry diseases, including hantavirus, which spreads when dried droppings are disturbed and particles get into the air. That's why sweeping or vacuuming with a regular vacuum is a bad idea.

Urine also soaks into insulation and wood, leaving odors that keep drawing other rodents to the same spot. A proper cleanup removes the contamination, not just the visible mess.

What should happen before cleanup starts?

  1. Remove the rodents. Trapping and removal come first. Cleaning while they're still active is wasted effort.
  2. Find and seal entry points. Common spots in San Diego homes include roof vents, gaps at the eaves, openings around pipes and wires, and torn foundation or gable screens.
  3. Trim back vegetation. Tree branches and vines touching the roof give rats an easy path up.
  4. Ventilate. Open the attic hatch and any vents for at least half an hour before going in.

How do you clean up rodent droppings safely?

For small areas of droppings, follow these steps:

  1. Put on rubber or nitrile gloves, eye protection and a properly fitted N95 or better respirator.
  2. Spray droppings, urine spots and nesting material with a disinfectant or a fresh bleach and water solution until thoroughly wet.
  3. Let it soak for several minutes, following the product label.
  4. Wipe up the waste with paper towels and place it in a sealed plastic bag.
  5. Disinfect the area again and wipe down hard surfaces.
  6. Double-bag all waste and dispose of it with household trash.
  7. Disinfect gloves before removing them, then wash your hands well.

If you find a dead rodent, spray it with disinfectant, let it soak, then pick it up with gloved hands or a bag and seal it inside a second bag.

Does insulation need to be replaced after rodents?

Usually, yes. Rodents tunnel through insulation, nest in it and soak it with urine. Contaminated insulation holds odors and can't be effectively cleaned. Professional crews remove it with commercial vacuums that bag the debris outside the home, then sanitize the attic surfaces.

Once the attic is clean and dry, new insulation goes in. That also gives you a chance to bring older, thin insulation up to a more useful depth, which helps comfort on both hot inland days and cool coastal nights.

What about the ductwork in the attic?

Many San Diego homes have ducts running through the attic, and rodents often chew or nest in flexible duct. A torn duct can pull contaminated attic air into the house every time the heat or AC runs. During cleanup, every duct run should be checked for damage, droppings and disconnected joints.

Damaged sections should be repaired or replaced, and if rodents got inside the ducts, a duct cleaning is a good idea once the attic is clean.

When should you hire professionals?

Call a professional crew when:

  • Droppings are spread through much of the attic
  • Insulation is heavily soiled or matted
  • There's a strong odor in the house
  • Ducts or wiring have been chewed
  • You aren't comfortable moving through a hot, tight attic

Our attic cleaning and rodent cleanup service covers insulation removal, sanitizing, entry point sealing and new insulation, and we can check the ductwork at the same time.

How do you keep rodents from coming back?

  • Keep roof vent and gable screens in good repair
  • Seal gaps around pipes, cables and AC line sets where they enter the house
  • Keep branches trimmed several feet from the roof
  • Store pet food and birdseed in sealed containers
  • Pick up fallen fruit from backyard trees
  • Check the attic with a flashlight every few months

Roof rats are common in many San Diego County neighborhoods, especially near fruit trees and dense landscaping. A little upkeep goes a long way toward keeping them out. If you hear scratching overhead again, act quickly, since a few new droppings are far easier to deal with than a second full cleanup.
faqs: Is it safe to vacuum rodent droppings?
Not with a regular household vacuum. It can stir dried particles into the air. Soak droppings with disinfectant and wipe them up, or have professionals remove them with proper equipment.
How long does attic rodent cleanup take?
It depends on the size of the attic and how much insulation needs removing. Many jobs take one to two days, including sanitizing and new insulation.
Will the smell go away after rodent cleanup?
Once contaminated insulation and nesting material are removed and the attic is sanitized, the odor usually clears. If it lingers, there may be a dead rodent or contamination in a wall or duct.
Should I clean the ducts after rodents in the attic?
If rodents damaged or got inside the ductwork, yes. Repair any torn ducts first, then clean the system so debris isn't blown into living spaces.
